title: Check-in
style: cinematic horror film still, dramatic moody lighting, lonely 1970s roadside motel at night in the rain, buzzing pink neon and sodium orange glow against deep blue darkness, wood paneling and worn carpet, film grain, 35mm, highly detailed, subject clearly visible, no text, no watermark
caption:
Part 4. He came back thirty years older. He asked for his usual. 🗝️

Original fiction. Part 5 tomorrow night.

#scarystories #horrorstory #creepy #storytime #fyp

scenes.narration: Last time: the old night clerk told Marcus that Room 9 isn't a room. It's a waiting list. And he's on it.
scenes.image: a man sitting alone in his parked car outside a dark motel, rain on the windshield

scenes.narration: Marcus went to work anyway. Where else do you go? He locked the office, turned the radio up, and sat facing the window.
scenes.image: a man behind a motel desk at night staring out a rain-streaked window, an old radio glowing beside him

scenes.narration: At 1:40, headlights. The same grey raincoat. The same slow walk through the rain.
scenes.image: headlights cutting through heavy rain in a motel parking lot, a figure in a long coat walking toward the office

scenes.narration: But the man was older. Thirty years older, overnight. White hair. Spotted hands. The same coat, dripping on the same carpet.
scenes.image: an elderly man with white hair in a dripping grey raincoat standing in a motel office doorway

scenes.narration: He smiled like they were old friends. Evening, Marcus. My usual.
scenes.image: close-up of the old man's kind, tired smile under the motel office lamp, rain on his shoulders

scenes.narration: Marcus said Room 9 was closed. The man laughed softly. It's never closed. You've been keeping it warm for me.
scenes.image: two men facing each other across a wood-paneled counter at night, a neon glow between them

scenes.narration: Marcus looked at the key board. The hook for Room 9 was empty. The key was already on the counter. Between them.
scenes.image: an old brass motel key lying alone on a wooden counter in lamplight, a faint wisp of steam rising from it

scenes.narration: He picked it up. It was warm. Not pocket warm. Hand warm. Like someone had been holding it for a very long time.
scenes.image: a man's palm holding an old brass key, his fingers trembling, warm light

scenes.narration: The old man leaned in. His breath smelled like rain and motel soap. Check the book, son.
scenes.image: an old man leaning across a motel counter close to a younger man's ear, shadows deep

scenes.narration: Under Marcus's name, fresh ink. The checkout line, finally filled in. Tomorrow night. 2 AM.
scenes.image: close-up of fresh glistening ink on an old guestbook page, illegible handwriting, the lamp flickering
